sentences.text:
Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:150383
Court No. - 70
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 21840 of 2024

Applicant :- Smt Kiran
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

Counsel for Applicant :- Ashutosh Kumar Tiwari,Faizan Siddiqui
Counsel for Opposite Party :- Amit Rana,G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.

Heard Sri Deepak Pandey, learned Advocate holding brief of Sri Ashutosh Kumar Tiwari, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Amit Rana, learned counsel for the informant and Dr. S.B. Maurya,
learned AGA-I for the State.
2.

The instant bail application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No. 45 of 2024, under Sections 420, 406, 467, 468, 471, 120B IPC, Police Station Medical, District Meerut during pendency of the trial.

3. FIR of the present case was lodged against applicant and her husband Neeraj Kumar and according to the FIR co-accused Neeraj Kumar made contact with the informant and told him that he along with his wife i.e. applicant runs a firm with the name and style Newex Capital and his firm indulged in the business to provide loan to the companies and he can provide loan to the informant and under the pretext to provide loan to the firm of the informant, he got transferred Rs.
19,75,000/- in the account of the firm through RTGS.

It is further mentioned in the FIR that a cheque was also given by the firm Newex Capital to the informant but signature on the cheque were Smt Kiran vs State Of U.P. on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199849114/
1 forged one.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that applicant is however proprietor of the alleged firm Newex Capital but she is household lady and having no concern with day-to-day business of the firm and her husband on her behalf did entire business and only being his wife, she used to put her signature on the documents provided by her husband i.e. co-accused Neeraj Kumar.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He further submits that this fact has specifically been mentioned by the applicant in paragraph-8 to the supplementary affidavit filed in support of instant bail application.

5. He further submits that even from perusal of the FIR, it reflects that husband of the applicant was principal accused, who committed fraud and cheating and merely being proprietor of the firm applicant has been made accused in the present matter.

6. He further submits that applicant is a lady and she is having infant child of seven months and she is not having any criminal history and all the alleged offences are triable by Magistrate and in the present matter applicant is in jail since 08.04.2024 i.e. for last more than five months.
7.

Per contra, learned AGA as well as learned counsel for the informant opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that applicant was the sole proprietor of the firm and in her firm entire money was transferred and she provided a cheque to the informant and on the cheque the signature was forged one, therefore, it cannot be said that applicant was not having any concern with her proprietorship firm but both the counsels could not dispute the fact that even from the FIR it reflects that husband of the applicant was the person who induced the informant to transfer the money in the firm Newex Capital.
8.

They further could not dispute the fact that applicant is a lady and she is having seven months infant child and in the present matter she is in jail since 08.04.2024 i.e. for last more than five months.
9. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

10. However, as per allegation the husband of the applicant by playing fraud got transferred Rs.
19,75,000/- in the proprietorship firm Newex Capital in which applicant was the sole proprietor but considering the fact that applicant is a lady and is the wife of co-accused Neeraj Kumar, the submission advanced by learned counsel for the applicant and averment made in paragraph-8 to the supplementary affidavit cannot be brushed aside at this stage.
11. Further, applicant is a lady and she is also having seven months infant child and she is not having any criminal history.
12. Further, all the alleged offences are triable by Magistrate and in the present matter applicant is in jail since 08.04.2024 i.e. for last more than five months.

sentences.text: 13. Further, law is settled that bail is a rule while bail rejection is an exception and bail application should not be withheld for punitive purposes and unless proven guilty an accused should be deemed as innocent.

14. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view,
applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
15. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

16. Let the applicant - Smt Kiran be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
17. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

18. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
Order Date :- 13.9.2024 AK Pandey  Smt Kiran vs State Of U.P. on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199849114/
